event: After Elector Clemens August's death and Kapellmeister Touchemoulin's resignation, Louis van Beethoven becomes Kapellmeister at the Bonn court
Ludwig van Beethoven is born in Bonn
notes: Text says "probably"; no civil birth record exists, and the date is inferred from the baptism one day later

event: Baptism of Ludwig van Beethoven at St Remigius, Bonn; his birth is traditionally dated 16 December 1770
source: Baptismal register, St Remigius, Bonn; CAEYERS2020
notes: No birth certificate survives; the baptismal entry is the earliest documentary record.

event: Ludwig's grandfather Louis van Beethoven, Kapellmeister at the Bonn court, dies on Christmas Eve
notes: Beethoven was barely three years old

event: First documented public performance as a pianist (advertised age: six)
notes: Concert announcement gives the programme shared with other pupils of van Beethoven's father.

event: First published composition: Nine Variations on a March by Ernst Christoph Dressler, WoO 63
notes: Neefe's report of March 1783 already speaks of the set as published in Mannheim (Caeyers, ch. 4).

event: Beethoven is appointed Christian Gottlob Neefe's official deputy as court organist in Bonn
notes: The post was unpaid, as was customary for young "accessist" musicians serving a trial period

event: Beethoven travels with his mother to the Netherlands and gives several concerts
notes: Autumn 1783; the trip began as a family visit to relatives in Rotterdam

event: Christian Gottlob Neefe's report in Cramer's Magazin der Musik predicts Beethoven will become 'a second Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart'
source: Cramer, Magazin der Musik, 2 March 1783; CAEYERS2020

event: Beethoven performs a piano concerto at the Binnenhof in The Hague with the orchestra of Prince William V of Orange-Nassau under Christian Ernst Graaf
notes: He received sixty-three guilders, nearly half his later annual salary in Bonn

event: Appointed assistant organist at the Electoral court of Maximilian Franz
Beethoven becomes official deputy court organist in Bonn with an annual salary of 150 guilders
notes: His application, submitted in spring 1784, was delayed by Elector Maximilian Friedrich's death on 15 April 1784

event: Beethoven arrives in Vienna on his first journey there
notes: He left Bonn before the new year and arrived on or around 14 January after a journey of nearly one thousand kilometers

event: Beethoven meets Mozart in Vienna
notes: No meeting could have taken place before mid-February, when Mozart returned from Prague; Caeyers stresses that the accounts by Schindler and Jahn were written many years after Beethoven's death and must be treated with extreme caution, and that whether lessons took place is unknown

event: Beethoven leaves Vienna and returns toward Bonn via Munich, Regensburg, and Augsburg
notes: He left on 28 March at the latest, after a stay of over two months; in Augsburg he met the keyboard builder Johann Andreas Stein

event: Beethoven's mother, Maria Magdalena van Beethoven, dies in Bonn
Death of his mother, Maria Magdalena van Beethoven
Beethoven writes to Joseph von Schaden in Augsburg asking for more time to repay a loan from his Vienna journey
notes: The earliest surviving letter in Beethoven's own hand

event: Beethoven's only sister, Maria Margaretha, dies in Bonn at the age of one and a half
Beethoven enrolls at the University of Bonn to take courses in philosophy and classical literature
notes: He enrolled at the suggestion of his friends in the Zehrgarten circle

event: Beethoven receives an official contract as violist and Kammermusicus in the Bonn court orchestra
notes: Part of the expansion of the Kapelle following the reopening of the court theater on 3 January 1789

event: An electoral decree forces Jean van Beethoven into early retirement and transfers half of his family support payments to his eldest son Ludwig
notes: The measure was taken at Ludwig's own request, urged by Waldstein and the von Breuning family

event: Beethoven is commissioned to write a cantata on the accession of Emperor Leopold II
notes: This project likewise failed, and a planned performance at Mergentheim in autumn 1791 was cancelled; the cantata was never performed in his lifetime

event: The memorial service for Emperor Joseph II takes place in Bonn without Beethoven's funeral cantata, which could not be completed in time
notes: Beethoven received the final text only on 28 February 1790; minutes of 17 March record that the cantata could not be performed; it was never performed in his lifetime

event: Joseph Haydn, stopping in Bonn on his way to London, is introduced to Beethoven
notes: The introduction was arranged by Johann Salomon, whose family had longstanding ties to the Beethovens

event: Beethoven travels with the Bonn Kapelle to the Teutonic Order congress at Mergentheim and is praised in a review by Carl Ludwig Junker in Bossler's Musikalische Korrespondenz
notes: Autumn 1791, a three-month journey; en route in Aschaffenburg he performed his Righini Variations from memory and caricatured the playing of the pianist Johann Sterkel

event: Beethoven's Variations on Righini's "Venni amore" are published
notes: Described as recently published when Beethoven performed them from memory at Aschaffenburg in autumn 1791

event: Waldstein's Ritterballet premieres in the Redoutensaal in Bonn, with music ghostwritten by Beethoven
notes: The music was presented as Count Waldstein's own composition

event: On Haydn's return from London, Beethoven shows him one of his imperial cantatas in Bonn, and arrangements are made for Beethoven to travel to Vienna for lessons with Haydn
Count Waldstein writes the farewell entry in Beethoven's Stammbuch ('through unceasing diligence receive Mozart's spirit from Haydn's hands')
Leaves Bonn for Vienna to study with Joseph Haydn
Beethoven's friends hold a farewell party for him at the Zehrgarten in Bonn and present him with the Stammbuch
Beethoven leaves Bonn for Vienna very early in the morning
notes: The first leg ran through the war zone to Frankfurt in a single stretch

event: Beethoven arrived in Vienna.
Beethoven arrives in Vienna
notes: He never saw the city of his birth again

event: Death of his father, Johann van Beethoven
Beethoven accompanied Haydn to Eisenstadt in the summer and shadowed him while he worked on a London symphony and string quartets.
Beethoven commenced counterpoint lessons with Johann Albrechtsberger three times a week in the spring.
Beethoven accepted Karl von Lichnowsky's invitation to move from the ground floor to the first floor of his Alsergasse home.
Beethoven made a proposal of marriage to singer Magdalena Willmann.
notes: Text gives 1795 or at the very latest the spring of 1796

event: First public appearance in Vienna as pianist-composer (Burgtheater benefit concert)
notes: The concerto performed was an early version of either Op. 15 or Op. 19; the sources do not settle which.

event: Haydn attended the premiere of Beethoven's Piano Trios at the Lichnowskys'.
Beethoven's Piano Trios were released as his Opus 1 by Artaria and Co.
Beethoven performed his Piano Concerto in C Major at a benefit concert for Haydn in the small Redoutensaal.
Beethoven and Lichnowsky left Vienna early in February on a concert tour through Prague, Dresden, Leipzig and Berlin.
Beethoven returned to Vienna and fell seriously ill several days after his arrival.
notes: Source accounts differ on the cause, with Weissenbach diagnosing typhus and later linking it to irreversible hearing loss

event: Beethoven performed the First Piano Concerto in Pressburg.
Beethoven first noticed hearing problems that later spread from his right ear to his left ear.
Beethoven's song Adelaide was published.
Beethoven premiered his Quintet for Piano and Winds at a concert given by Schuppanzigh.
Prince Lobkowitz commissioned Beethoven to compose a set of six string quartets.
notes: Text places the commission in the autumn of 1798

event: Beethoven returned to Prague to give three public concerts.
notes: Text states these were his final performances abroad

event: Countess Anna von Brunsvik and her daughters Therese and Josephine first visited Beethoven at his apartment on Petersplatz.
notes: Text places the visit early in May 1799

event: Scores of the first three string quartets were copied and Beethoven gifted the String Quartet in F Major to Amenda.
First self-organised Akademie at the Burgtheater: premiere of Symphony No. 1 and the Septet
Beethoven and Giovanni Punto performed the Horn Sonata together at Punto's Akademie at the Hofburgtheater.
Beethoven and Giovanni Punto gave a second performance of the Horn Sonata.
Beethoven delivered the full set of six string quartets to Lobkowitz.
A concert in honour of the Duchess of Giovane featured the Violin Sonata in E-flat and several of the opus 18 string quartets.
Beethoven took ten-year-old Carl Czerny on as a pupil after an audition in Beethoven's apartment.
Beethoven and Giovanni Punto appeared together at a benefit concert organized by soprano Christine Gerhardi.
Beethoven and Magdalena Willmann gave a concert together in the Redoutensaal.
Beethoven's ballet The Creatures of Prometheus was premiered.
notes: Originally scheduled for March 21, 1801 and postponed by one week

event: Beethoven broke down after the initial Prometheus season ended.
Beethoven wrote to Amenda imploring him never to show the earlier version of the Quartet in F Major to anyone.
Letter to Franz Wegeler: earliest written testimony of his hearing loss and of an 'enchanting girl' he loves
notes: Caeyers identifies the girl as Giulietta Guicciardi, Beethoven's piano pupil and the dedicatee of Op. 27 No. 2.

event: Friedrich Rochlitz's initial effort to force a libretto on Beethoven ended in failure.
Beethoven wrote to Breitkopf & Härtel announcing his retreat and stating that his brother would manage his affairs.
Beethoven left for Heiligenstadt and took lodgings in a house on Herrengasse.
Heiligenstadt Testament written (signed 6 October, with a postscript of 10 October)
Beethoven receives word that Artaria is preparing an unauthorized edition of the String Quintet already sold to Breitkopf & Härtel
notes: Artaria had obtained a copy of the score before Count Fries's six-month exclusivity period had elapsed

event: Sébastien Erard gifts Beethoven a grand piano
notes: Beethoven believed Rodolphe Kreutzer had facilitated the gesture

event: Schikaneder appoints Beethoven "Composer at Theater an der Wien", with lodgings in the theater complex and an obligation to compose at least one new opera each year
Beethoven publishes a notice in the Wiener Zeitung declaring Artaria's edition of the String Quintet unauthorized and full of errors, and Breitkopf & Härtel's edition the authorized one
Akademie at the Theater an der Wien: premieres of Symphony No. 2, Piano Concerto No. 3 and Christus am Oelberge
Ferdinand Ries writes to publisher Nikolaus Simrock announcing Beethoven's plan to move to Paris within eighteen months
notes: Ries raised the plan twice more several months later

event: Beethoven receives the first version of Schikaneder's libretto Vestas Feuer
notes: He had waited six months for it and was mortified by its convoluted plot

event: Beethoven gives Josephine Deym the song "An die Hoffnung" in the autumn
notes: The song functioned as an unabashed declaration of love and was to be shown to no one

event: Beethoven has completely abandoned work on Schikaneder's Vestas Feuer by New Year's Day
notes: Only the opening scene was more or less complete; its finale was later recycled in Leonore

event: Initial rehearsals of the Third Symphony are held at Prince Lobkowitz's palace
notes: Financial records show an orchestra of twenty-seven players; Lobkowitz held exclusive performance rights, initially for six months

event: Josephine Deym, widowed in January, reestablishes contact with Beethoven, who resumes giving her piano lessons almost daily
The Third Symphony is performed privately for Prince Louis Ferdinand of Prussia during his stay with Lobkowitz
notes: Louis Ferdinand had the work played through three times in its entirety

event: Beethoven takes lodgings in the Pasqualatihaus on the Mölker Bastei
notes: The Pasqualatihaus remained his preferred residence over the next ten years

event: The Third Symphony is performed at a semiprivate concert at the home of banker Joseph Würth
notes: The first of two January concerts intended to prepare a select audience for the public premiere

event: The Third Symphony is performed at a second semiprivate concert in Lobkowitz's concert hall
First public performance of the Eroica, Theater an der Wien
The court case over Artaria's unauthorized edition of the String Quintet is finally closed
notes: Beethoven had been ordered on September 26, 1803 to retract his public declaration, and did so on March 31, 1804

event: The censors issue a ban on Leonore
notes: Sonnleithner appealed, arguing the warden's abuses were personal rather than systemic

event: The censors approve the Leonore libretto on condition that the "most flagrant scenes" be removed
notes: The text notes that no musical material was altered, so the condition must have concerned the spoken dialogue

event: Premiere of Leonore (first version of Fidelio), Theater an der Wien
notes: Vienna was under French occupation; the audience was small and largely military.

event: First performance of the revised Leonore (Leonore II), with cuts and restructuring by Stephan Breuning and a new overture
notes: The theater treated it as a revival; a dispute with Braun over compensation ended further performances after the second show on April 10, 1806

event: Kaspar Karl van Beethoven marries Johanna Reiss
notes: His marriage ended his four years as Beethoven's secretary and manager of his affairs

event: Beethoven resumes work on the three string quartets begun in the summer of 1804
notes: The date is marked in the autograph

event: Beethoven meets Count Franz von Oppersdorff at Oberlogau, where the count's orchestra performs the Second Symphony and he commissions two new symphonies
notes: Beethoven composed one completely new symphony (the Fourth) and never delivered the second

event: The Third Symphony is published in Vienna bearing the title Sinfonia Eroica, dedicated to Prince Lobkowitz
notes: All references to Napoleon had been removed; the title page adds that the work was composed to celebrate the memory of a great man

event: The three Razumovsky Quartets are completed
notes: First airings followed around New Year's Day 1807

event: Premiere of the Violin Concerto at Franz Clement's Akademie at Theater an der Wien
notes: The claim that Clement sight-read the solo part is described as most likely an exaggeration

event: Beethoven petitions the Theater an der Wien management to compose at least one major opera per year for a fixed annual salary of 2,400 guilders
notes: The proposal was rejected, though freelance engagements and an Akademie were left open

event: The newly founded Liebhaber-Konzerte proclaim Beethoven their composer in residence and invite him onto the programming committee
notes: The series opened on November 12, 1807 before an audience of over thirteen hundred

event: The Appassionata is published, dedicated to Franz von Brunsvik
notes: The title "Appassionata" was added only in 1838 by the Hamburg publisher Cranz

event: Two concerts at the Lobkowitz residence present all four symphonies composed so far, giving the first performance of the Fourth Symphony and the premiere of the Coriolan Overture
Gleichenstein concludes a contract giving Clementi the exclusive English rights to opp. 58–62 for two hundred pounds sterling
notes: The contract also commissioned a piano arrangement of the Violin Concerto and further piano works

event: Beethoven and Josephine Deym part for good after he returns from Eisenstadt and insists on a reunion
notes: Josephine refused to receive him, sending a servant to turn him away at the door

event: Premiere of the Mass in C, commissioned by Prince Nikolaus Esterházy for his wife's name-day celebrations
notes: The performance was under-rehearsed and displeased the prince

event: Beethoven writes to Count Oppersdorff that he has been offered the post of Kapellmeister in Kassel
notes: Reichardt's later claim to have made the offer himself, and to have advised against it, was publicly denied by Beethoven

event: Akademie at the Theater an der Wien: premieres of Symphonies No. 5 and No. 6, the Choral Fantasy, and the Vienna premiere of Piano Concerto No. 4
Fifth Piano Concerto completed
notes: Drafted before the war and completed in the summer of 1809

event: Beethoven writes to Breitkopf & Härtel claiming he has officially accepted the Kassel Kapellmeister offer
notes: Meanwhile Gleichenstein used the Kassel contract as leverage to negotiate terms keeping Beethoven in Vienna

event: Annuity agreement signed by Archduke Rudolph, Prince Kinsky and Prince Lobkowitz to keep Beethoven in Vienna
Beethoven presents Das Lebewohl for piano to Archduke Rudolph as a parting gift on the imperial family's flight from Vienna
During the French bombardment of Vienna on the night of May 11, Beethoven takes refuge in the cellar of his brother Kaspar Karl's house on Rauhensteingasse
notes: He sat for hours with his head and oversensitive ears buried in a pile of cushions

event: String Quartet in F minor composed
notes: Composed in the autumn of 1810; its public debut came only in 1814 and publication in 1816

event: Beethoven adds Abwesenheit and Das Wiedersehn on Archduke Rudolph's return, completing the sonata Les Adieux
Beethoven's incidental music to Goethe's Egmont is first performed, at the play's fourth performance
notes: The play itself had premiered on 24 May 1810 without the music, which was finished late

event: Beethoven travels to Teplitz for the first spa stay of his life
notes: The Pest theater commission arrived the day before his scheduled departure on 1 August

event: Beethoven announces that he has sent off the completed scores of King Stephan and The Ruins of Athens for the opening of the new theater in Pest
Fifth Piano Concerto premiered by Friedrich Schneider at the Gewandhaus
notes: Beethoven never performed the concerto publicly himself

event: Viennese premiere of the Fifth Piano Concerto with Carl Czerny as soloist
notes: Reception was lukewarm owing to the society-event circumstances, not the soloist or work

event: King Stephan and The Ruins of Athens premiered at the opening of the new imperial theater in Pest
notes: The premiere was postponed from 4 October 1811 because of incomplete construction work, not any delay by Beethoven

event: Beethoven meets Prince Kinsky in Prague and settles the terms of payment under the annuity decree
The letter to the 'Immortal Beloved' is written in Teplitz (6-7 July 1812)
notes: The addressee is not named in the letter. The dataset records the document, not any candidate identification.

event: Beethoven and Goethe meet for the first time in Teplitz
Beethoven and Goethe meet in September for what proves to be their final encounter
notes: The two never corresponded again, apart from Beethoven's unanswered letter of February 1823

event: Beethoven arrives back in Teplitz and continues work on his Eighth Symphony
Beethoven puts the finishing touches on the Seventh and Eighth Symphonies
News reaches Beethoven of the death of Prince Kinsky, dashing hopes of prompt payment under the 1809 decree
Violin Sonata in G major first performed by Archduke Rudolph and Pierre Rode at the Lobkowitz residence
notes: The parts had been collected from Beethoven, still wet, only two days earlier

event: Kaspar Karl van Beethoven signs a will appointing his brother Ludwig as guardian of his son Karl
notes: Kaspar Karl lived a further two and a half years; the will may have been signed under pressure, as Beethoven loaned him a large sum the same day

event: Premiere of Symphony No. 7 and Wellingtons Sieg at a benefit concert for wounded soldiers (University hall)
Piano Sonata in E minor composed
notes: Composed in the summer of 1814, during the Fidelio revival; the first sonata in which Beethoven used extended German tempo descriptions

event: Beethoven gives an Akademie of his own works in the Redoutensaal, including Wellington's Victory and selections from The Ruins of Athens
Beethoven engages Georg Friedrich Treitschke to revise the libretto of Leonore
notes: The revision took over two months

event: Eighth Symphony receives its first public performance, on a program with the Seventh Symphony and Wellington's Victory
notes: A critic judged the Eighth overshadowed by the Seventh

event: Premiere of Die gute Nachricht, a singspiel celebrating the fall of Napoleon, with a finale contributed by Beethoven
notes: Treitschke's text celebrated the capitulation of Paris; Beethoven collaborated free of charge alongside Gyrowetz, Hummel, Kanne and Weigl

event: Premiere of Fidelio in its final version, Kaerntnertortheater
Beethoven gives his own benefit performance of Fidelio
Congress Akademie in the Redoutensaal before the assembled dignitaries, with the premiere of Der glorreiche Augenblick alongside the Seventh Symphony and Wellington's Victory
notes: The concert had been rescheduled three times; a repeat without the monarchs three days later drew poorly and a third concert was cancelled

event: Meeresstille und glückliche Fahrt, a setting of two Goethe poems, composed
notes: Composed on the heels of the Congress occasional works in 1815

event: Wellington's Victory is performed at the Theatre Royal, Drury Lane, from the score Beethoven had sent to the Prince Regent
notes: The Prince Regent never replied to Beethoven or reimbursed the cost of the score

event: Death of his brother Kaspar Karl; the guardianship dispute over Karl begins
Beethoven is named an honorary citizen of Vienna
Beethoven completes the Piano Sonata in A Major
Beethoven completes the song cycle An die ferne Geliebte
notes: Shortly before publication he altered the title from "die entfernte Geliebte" to "die ferne Geliebte"

event: The Landgericht rules that Johanna van Beethoven be denied all custody of her son Karl
notes: Beethoven signed the official guardianship documents ten days later; the court had initially awarded Beethoven and Johanna dual custody a week after Kaspar Karl's death

event: Steiner publishes Wellington's Victory in seven different versions simultaneously
notes: Beethoven's first orchestral score published together with its orchestral parts

event: A catarrh infection develops into chronic bronchitis that plagues Beethoven until June 1817
notes: The text notes it is unclear whether pneumonia was present from the beginning

event: Beethoven conducts his Seventh Symphony in the Redoutensaal despite his illness
Ferdinand Ries conveys the London Philharmonic Society's offer of 300 guineas for Beethoven to travel to London in the winter of 1817-18 and compose and conduct two symphonies
notes: Beethoven demanded a larger advance and a travel allowance; the society refused on 19 August 1817 and the plan lapsed

event: Beethoven works on the Piano Sonata in B-flat Major (the Hammerklavier Sonata)
Conversation books begin: written exchanges become necessary as his hearing fails
notes: The surviving conversation books (from 1818) are a principal source for the last decade.

event: Karl van Beethoven comes to live permanently with his uncle
notes: He had spent over two years at the Giannattasio del Rio boarding school in Landstrasse

event: Karl flees his school to take refuge with his mother
notes: Beethoven had the police remove him from her home several days later

event: Beethoven begins work on the Missa solemnis for Archduke Rudolph's installation as archbishop of Olmütz, scheduled for March 1820
notes: The Mass was not finished in time; Rudolph instead used Hummel's Mass in B-flat and a Te Deum by Joseph Preindl, and the date of that decision is unknown

event: Beethoven composes the Diabelli Variations
notes: After sketching twenty-three variations in 1819 he set the work aside for nearly three years

event: Joint custody of Karl is awarded to his mother and Mathias von Tuscher, and Karl is removed from Beethoven's care
notes: Tuscher resigned the guardianship after three months

event: The Hammerklavier Sonata is published by Artaria in Vienna
notes: An English edition followed in London two months later, split into two parts at Beethoven's own suggestion

event: The appellate court rules in favor of Beethoven and Karl Peters as Karl's guardians
notes: Johanna's two further appeals, one to the emperor himself, failed

event: Beethoven is bedridden for six weeks with a rheumatic episode in the spring and incapacitated for a further six weeks by jaundice in the summer
notes: The text suggests the jaundice may have been an early symptom of a chronic liver condition

event: Beethoven completes the Piano Sonata in A-flat Major around Christmas
The Piano Sonata in C Minor is ready for delivery to the publisher Schlesinger by mid-February
Rossini visits Beethoven at his lodgings on Landstrasser Hauptstrasse
notes: The account derives from Rossini's later recollections to Wagner, recorded by Edmond Michotte

event: The Consecration of the House overture is premiered at the opening of the new theatre in Josefstadt, with Beethoven directing from the piano
Fidelio is revived in Vienna with Wilhelmine Schröder making her debut as Leonore
The London Philharmonic Society agrees to commission a grand symphony from Beethoven for fifty pounds, with exclusive rights for eighteen months
notes: Beethoven protested the fee and repeatedly shifted the deadline

event: Missa solemnis completed
Beethoven signs a will and testament leaving everything to his nephew Karl and explicitly excluding his brother Johann
Beethoven suffers a serious eye condition, identified by modern specialists as uveitis, that restricts his reading and writing
notes: The symptoms resurfaced in January 1826

event: Beethoven composes the Ninth Symphony
Beethoven spends a day with Carl Maria von Weber at Baden
notes: The two composers' conversation was written on a slate and wiped away; Weber described the day in a letter to his wife that evening

event: First complete performance of the Missa solemnis, St Petersburg (Prince Galitzin's concert)
Premiere of Symphony No. 9, with movements of the Missa solemnis, Kaerntnertortheater
The Ninth Symphony is performed a second time, with only the Kyrie retained from the Missa solemnis
notes: The hall was only half full, most of the nobility having left Vienna for the countryside

event: Beethoven completes the String Quartet in E-flat Major, the first of the quartets commissioned by Prince Galitzin
notes: Galitzin's commission, requesting one to three quartets, was sent from St. Petersburg on 9 November 1822

event: Premiere of the String Quartet Op. 127 (Schuppanzigh Quartet)
Beethoven announces the completion of the String Quartet in A Minor
notes: Its slow movement, the "Hymn of thanks from a convalescent to the deity, in the Lydian mode," followed his recovery from a serious gastrointestinal illness in April and May 1825 under Dr. Braunhofer's strict dietary regime

event: Beethoven moves into the Schwarzspanierhaus in Alservorstadt, his last official address
The String Quartet in A Minor receives its official premiere, with Karl Holz playing first violin in Schuppanzigh's absence
The String Quartet in B-flat Major, the third Galitzin quartet, is completed
notes: The text states the quartet was ready before Christmas 1825, with the Grosse Fuge as its finale

event: Nephew Karl attempts suicide (late July / early August 1826) and survives
Karl van Beethoven shoots himself in the head at the Rauhenstein castle ruins in the Helenental near Baden and survives
notes: The second bullet bounced off his temple; at his own request he was taken to his mother's house

event: Beethoven completes the String Quartet in F Major, his final quartet
notes: In a letter to Schlesinger dated 30 October 1826 he reports that the quartet, especially the last movement, had been an arduous undertaking

event: Beethoven abruptly leaves Gneixendorf with Karl, travelling two days in an open carriage in wind and rain
notes: He returned to Vienna gravely ill; Johann had refused him the use of a closed carriage

event: Beethoven composes the canon "Wir irren allesamt" (We all make mistakes)
notes: The text identifies this canon, written while Karl Holz was persuading him to accept Wawruch, as the last music Beethoven ever wrote

event: Professor Wawruch begins treating Beethoven, three days after his return to Vienna
notes: Other doctors had declined; the text disputes Schindler's claim that Karl caused the delay

event: The first abdominal puncture (paracentesis) is performed on Beethoven by Dr. Seibert
Beethoven has his will of 1823 authenticated, expressly designating Karl as sole beneficiary, the day before Karl's final farewell
The fourth and final abdominal puncture is performed; thereafter Beethoven's treatment is purely palliative
Beethoven writes his last letter, an arrears notice to Prince Galitzin's banker in St. Petersburg
notes: Galitzin never paid the outstanding fees for the quartets in Beethoven's lifetime; the debt was settled only in 1852

event: A priest administers the last rites to Beethoven
notes: A codicil to his will had been signed the previous day; Schindler reports that after the priest left, Beethoven said "Plaudite amici, comoedia finita est"

event: Death of Ludwig van Beethoven at the Schwarzspanierhaus
Funeral in Waehring; Franz Grillparzer's funeral oration is read by the actor Heinrich Anschuetz
notes: Contemporary reports describe a crowd of many thousands; exact attendance figures vary by source.

event: Remains transferred from Waehring to the Central Cemetery (Zentralfriedhof), Vienna
notes: Posthumous entry: included because reference works routinely close the chronology with it.
